prompt: When can a binary relation on a set $A$ be both reflexive and irreflexive?

answers.explanation: On the empty domain both universal conditions hold vacuously. Any element in a nonempty domain would require and forbid its loop.

answers.text: For every domain, by choosing the empty relation.
answers.explanation: On a nonempty domain the empty relation is not reflexive.

answers.text: For every domain, by choosing the identity relation.
answers.explanation: Identity has loops on every element and is not irreflexive when the domain is nonempty.
The empty domain has no element that could violate either universal condition.

answers.text: Exactly when the relation has no off-diagonal pairs.
answers.explanation: The conflict concerns loops, not off-diagonal pairs.
The sole loop would have to be both present and absent.

answers.text: Exactly when the relation is symmetric.
answers.explanation: Symmetry says nothing about the required conflict on loops.

answers.text: Exactly when at least one element lacks a loop.
answers.explanation: Irreflexivity requires every loop to be absent; reflexivity requires all of them.

answers.text: Exactly when the relation is antisymmetric.
answers.explanation: Antisymmetry allows loops; it does not make reflexivity compatible with irreflexivity.

answers.text: Exactly when all related elements are distinct.
answers.explanation: That condition is irreflexivity alone and can hold on nonempty domains.
